summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, kidney transplantation, and breast cancer was admitted for a persistent cough, fatigue, and myalgias lasting several weeks, initially treated with antibiotics without improvement. Evaluation revealed normal white blood cell count, stable chronic lung changes on CT, and negative respiratory viral panels. A sputum culture was invalid due to contamination. Given her immunocompromised status and orthostatic symptoms, concern for adrenal insufficiency prompted a short course of stress-dose prednisone despite a normal cortisol level. Her condition improved with supportive care, including IV fluids and symptom management. She was discharged home when stable, with instructions to follow up on pending EBV and CMV tests and resume her baseline medications, including returning to her home prednisone dose.
